description: Sothis is a team of Egyptian software engineers, researchers, and UI/UX designers at NASA Space Apps. Inspired by Sothis (Sirius)—the star that guided ancient Egyptian astronomy—we bridge history with tech. Our pixel-pyramid logo represents this fusion of ancient precision and modern data. So, this is Sothis: fusing cosmic roots with scalable tech to solve Earth and space challenges, one pixel at a time.
summary:
When floods strike under thick storm clouds or wildfires rage beneath dense smoke, optical satellites go blind—hiding critical changes on Earth's surface when communities need clarity most. Sothis Echo is a bilingual (English/Arabic) interactive web platform built for the Dancing with the SARs challenge that turns real NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar data into an intuitive, human-centered story.
Rather than overwhelming users with raw scientific files, our platform guides students, educators, and researchers through real post-launch events—the 2026 Central Vietnam floods and West Attica wildfires—using four core experiences: an optical-vs-radar comparison slider, pixel-level before/after change detection maps backed by official NASA ASF granule IDs, a gamified "Radar Detective" module, and data sonification that lets users literally hear surface changes over time.
By combining transparent science with accessible storytelling, Sothis Echo bridges the gap between complex synthetic aperture radar physics and everyday situational awareness for learners and decision-makers worldwide.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Sothis Echo translates complex synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission into an interactive, story-driven web experience. Instead of presenting overwhelming scientific dashboards, we guide users through real post-launch events—the September 2026 Central Vietnam floods and the July 2026 West Attica wildfires in Greece—using five core modules:

  1. Camera vs. Radar Interactive Slider: Users drag a divider across the exact same geographic window to compare a cloud-obscured Sentinel-2 optical scene with a clear NISAR L-band radar image, instantly seeing how radar penetrates weather and darkness.
  2. Before/After & Pixel-Level Change Detection: For each disaster, users inspect geo-referenced NISAR L-band scenes alongside a computed pixel-by-pixel difference map (|After - Before| in dB). This highlights exact flood inundation zones and wildfire burn scars that are difficult for the human eye to spot in raw radar imagery.
  3. Radar Sonification (Hear the Dance): We map 16 sequential satellite passes to musical pitch, rhythm, and acoustic texture—allowing users to literally hear the sudden spike of a flood or the abrupt drop of a forest canopy fire.
  4. Recovery Clock: Using linear interpolation on real backscatter time series, users can adjust a target recovery slider (50%–95%) to estimate how many days an ecosystem takes to return to its pre-event baseline.
  5. Radar Detective Game: A two-round interactive challenge where players analyze real VV and VH polarization signals to diagnose ground events before evidence is revealed.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Our primary goal is clarity and accessibility. By explaining not just what changed on Earth's surface, but why the radar signal changed (such as double-bounce reflections from flooded tree trunks or the loss of volume scattering after a crown fire), Sothis Echo builds scientific intuition. It serves both high school students (ages 12–18) exploring Earth observation for the first time and researchers who can toggle Researcher Mode to inspect dB tables, acquisition parameters, and export CSV/JSON datasets.

Tools, Data & Technology

  • Frontend: Built with React 19, Vite, and Palantir Blueprint v6 (Light Mode), styled with a clean Tech Editorial aesthetic (Newsreader, Space Grotesk, and JetBrains Mono) with full English and Arabic (RTL) support.
  • Backend & Geospatial Pipeline: A custom Node.js serverless API that fetches and crops real NASA NISAR L-band (L2 GCOV browse) imagery from NASA ASF DAAC using official KML/WKT footprints, displaying the exact NASA Granule ID and acquisition timestamp under every scene. We complement NISAR imagery with real Sentinel-1 GRD (VV/VH) time-series processing from AWS Open Data and Sentinel-2 optical scenes for multi-sensor cross-validation.
  • Testing & Deployment: Deployed on Vercel with end-to-end automated testing via Playwright.

Creativity & Team Considerations

We combined cross-disciplinary expertise—bringing together frontend/backend engineering, dedicated scientific research, and visual design—to make radar physics approachable. Our key considerations were:

  • Scientific Honesty: We transparently label measured satellite data versus illustrative baselines, and we deliberately placed our Greece wildfire study window inland (Agios Vasileios / Mount Pateras) to avoid wind-driven sea backscatter noise.
  • Linguistic & Regional Inclusion: Providing a native Arabic (RTL) experience alongside English opens NASA Earth science to students and communities across Egypt, the Nile Basin, and the wider MENA region.
